The lateral-line system is a sensory system found in fish and aquatic amphibians that detects water movement, pressure changes, and nearby objects. It consists of specialized sensory organs called neuromasts arranged along the sides of the body and head. These neuromasts contain hair cells that respond to water displacement and pressure waves, allowing the animal to sense water currents, detect approaching predators or prey, navigate in murky water, maintain position in schools, and perceive obstacles or boundaries in their aquatic environment.
